scope: product copy only (brain/musterbriefe/templates via tools/pack-brain.py); the read-only archive /workspace/schreibdienst/musterbriefe is never modified
rule: Near-duplicate = (a) title token-set Jaccard >= 0.75, OR (b) title difflib ratio >= 0.75, OR (c) Klinik-section token-set Jaccard >= 0.90. The automated pass over the 152 manifest entries yields 11 pairs; each candidate is then reviewed against the manifest. Pairs describing clinically DISTINCT entities (e.g. Type 1 vs dialysis-dependent renal failure, different OP techniques) are NOT merged and are listed under non_merges. Groups below were additionally confirmed by Mohamed's 2026-10-02 decision (near-duplicates must be merged).

groups.title: Erysipel (Wundrose)
groups.reason: Identical indication keywords (Erysipel, Wundrose, Hautinfektion); one entity, two titles.

groups.title: pAVK / Mediasklerose
groups.reason: Mediasklerose is a diagnostic special case (unusable ABI) of the same pAVK entity; both share the keyword 'periphere arterielle Verschlusskrankheit'.

groups.title: Narbenhernien (epigastrisch)
groups.reason: Both describe an epigastric scar hernia; the IPOM file is a concrete case variant of the same entity.

groups.title: Pankreatitis (biliär / papillär)
groups.reason: Biliary and papillary pancreatitis share the same entity (Pankreatitis); the papillary file adds ERCP/papillotomy detail.

groups.title: Diabetes mellitus (Typ 1 / Typ 2)
groups.reason: Title token-set similarity 1.0 — the two files are structurally near-identical; merged into one template that keeps both type-specific statements.

groups.title: Kontusion der Zehen
groups.reason: Three near-identical toe-contusion templates (Kleinzehe/Mittelzehe body similarity 0.95; Grosszehe title ratio 0.59).

groups.title: Kontusion Grundgelenk Finger
groups.reason: Title ratio 0.92 / body similarity 0.66 — the same contusion template for two adjacent fingers.

non_merges.reason: Clinically distinct (dialysis yes/no), deliberately kept separate per the manifest's own sectionstats note.
Two distinct operative techniques; deliberately kept as two templates.
Gallbladder stones vs bile-duct stones — distinct entities; Cholezystolithiasis is additionally scrub-pending/locked.
Different injury aetiologies (needle-stick / stab / bite) that only share the generic word 'Verletzung'; not merged.
Different exposures (insect vs tick) with different prophylaxis; only title-part similarity.
Different metatarsals (V vs II); distinct fracture entities.
Different joints (thumb vs ankle); merging would destroy joint-specific management.
Distinct anatomical regions/entities; not near-duplicates of the merged toe/finger groups.
